deliverables.title: Why Titanic Did Not Have Enough Lifeboats
deliverables.hook: Titanic had twenty lifeboats. They couldn't save everyone aboard.
deliverables.narration: Titanic had twenty lifeboats. They couldn't save everyone aboard. The official British investigation counted two thousand two hundred and one people on the ship. But all twenty boats combined had room for only eleven hundred and seventy-eight. Fourteen were standard lifeboats, two were smaller emergency boats, and four were collapsibles. Even if every seat had been filled, more than a thousand people would still have lacked a place. And during the confusion, several boats left partly empty. The problem wasn't just the iceberg. It was also a rescue system that could never evacuate everyone. For the full story, watch our Titanic documentary. Subscribe to Facts Uncovered for more history.

deliverables.title: A Piece of Titanic Disappeared — And a Statue Returned
deliverables.hook: Titanic's wreck is changing before our eyes.
deliverables.narration: Titanic's wreck is changing before our eyes. In twenty twenty-four, an expedition found that a fifteen-foot section of railing had fallen from the port side of the ship's famous bow. The same expedition rediscovered a bronze statuette of the goddess Diana in the debris field. The deep ocean is slowly changing what remains of Titanic. And while a detailed digital survey was carried out in twenty twenty-two, its findings reached a wider audience in twenty twenty-five. Those images are new evidence, but they cannot tell us everything about the final night. See how historians investigate the wreck in our full Titanic documentary. Subscribe to Facts Uncovered for more historical discoveries.
